uas-100.title: Paper aircraft: test one change at a time
uas-100.plan:
Objective
Explain how lift, weight, thrust, and drag affect a paper aircraft.

Prepare
Paper, tape, ruler, marked flight area. Check equipment, supervision requirements, and the previous lesson record before class.

0–10 min · Brief and retrieve
Ask students to explain the relevant prior skill. Agree on today’s objective and how success will be demonstrated.

10–25 min · Explain and demonstrate
Introduce the essential vocabulary and demonstrate the first step. Ask students to predict the result before showing it.

25–65 min · Guided practice
Build a baseline paper airplane. Record three flights from the same launch point. Change one wing or trim feature, repeat three flights, and compare average distance and flight stability.

65–80 min · Demonstrate and assess
The student identifies the changed variable, presents both sets of measurements, and supports a conclusion with evidence. Record individual evidence; participation alone does not award a skill.

80–90 min · Debrief and reset
Compare predictions with results. Record one next step, save the work, and restore the learning area.

Optional homework
Sketch an improvement and predict its effect before the next test.

Instructor-review draft · Adapt pacing to the students.
Source: https://app.notion.com/p/Knowledge-Base-Courses-5fd9648b807a8345a9d80183a7c7460c

eng-101.title: Plan a combat robot
eng-101.plan:
Objective
Compare robot archetypes and select a design against an agreed classroom brief.

Prepare
Paper, dimensional limits, approved kit parts, Onshape. Check equipment, supervision requirements, and the previous lesson record before class.

0–10 min · Brief and retrieve
Ask students to explain the relevant prior skill. Agree on today’s objective and how success will be demonstrated.

10–25 min · Explain and demonstrate
Introduce the essential vocabulary and demonstrate the first step. Ask students to predict the result before showing it.

25–65 min · Guided practice
Compare a wedge, lifter, and other instructor-approved design using mass, traction, reach, and repairability. Sketch a layout, allocate component space, and document the selected concept. Powered mechanisms remain disabled during planning.

65–80 min · Demonstrate and assess
The student presents a dimensioned layout, a parts list, and a reasoned comparison against the class constraints. Record individual evidence; participation alone does not award a skill.

80–90 min · Debrief and reset
Compare predictions with results. Record one next step, save the work, and restore the learning area.

Optional homework
Measure the supplied components and update the layout.

eng-101.title: Onshape foundations
eng-101.plan:
Objective
Create and revise a dimensioned part with an editable feature history.

Prepare
Onshape, paper, ruler. Check equipment, supervision requirements, and the previous lesson record before class.

0–10 min · Brief and retrieve
Ask students to explain the relevant prior skill. Agree on today’s objective and how success will be demonstrated.

10–25 min · Explain and demonstrate
Introduce the essential vocabulary and demonstrate the first step. Ask students to predict the result before showing it.

25–65 min · Guided practice
Sketch a dimensioned mounting plate, extrude it, add mounting holes, and use a named variable for one repeated dimension. Change the variable, inspect the rebuild, and export a test part in millimeters.

65–80 min · Demonstrate and assess
The student demonstrates an intentional dimension change, explains the Feature list, and verifies the export scale. Record individual evidence; participation alone does not award a skill.

80–90 min · Debrief and reset
Compare predictions with results. Record one next step, save the work, and restore the learning area.

Optional homework
Save a version and annotate one model screenshot.
